title: Demurrage & Storage Calculator Video Guide: Watch Andrii Walk Through Real Calculations
meta_title: Demurrage & Storage Calculator Video Guide | SeaRates
meta_description: Watch our video guide on the Demurrage & Storage Calculator. See real examples of demurrage, detention, and storage fees calculated step by step.
body_markdown:
A container sits at the terminal after the free period runs out, and the meter starts running. Demurrage, then storage, maybe detention once the box leaves the port. For a lot of teams this only shows up when the invoice lands, which is exactly the problem the Demurrage & Storage Calculator was built to fix.

We put together a short video guide on our YouTube channel, where the team walks through real calculations of demurrage, detention, and storage fees, one step at a time. No theory dumps.

## Who presents it

Andrii Gorodynskyi, Digital Account Manager at SeaRates, takes you through the tool. The walkthrough stays practical rather than academic.

## What the calculator helps you do

The video shows how the tool supports day-to-day work with container shipping costs:

- Estimate time-related charges for containers before they hit your invoice
- Avoid unexpected demurrage and storage costs in your logistics operations
- Understand how free days, daily rates, and key dates shape the final amount you pay
- Plan a logistics budget with fewer surprises baked in
- Give your logistics team a quick way to check potential demurrage, detention, and storage fees as part of their digital toolkit, for any shipment

That last point matters more than it looks. When anyone on the team can model per diem charges and time-based fees on their own, questions about cost stop waiting on someone else to answer them.

## Free days, daily rates, key dates

Every port and carrier handles free days differently, and daily rates stack up fast once they expire. The calculator lets you map those inputs against your shipment's actual dates so the final invoice stops being a mystery. Logistics budget planning gets a lot easier when you can see the charges forming instead of receiving them.
